artists.biography:
Stone Temple Pilots (often abbreviated to STP) is an American rock band from San Diego, California that consists of Scott Weiland (lead vocals), brothers Robert DeLeo (bass guitar, vocals) and Dean DeLeo (guitar), and Eric Kretz (drums, percussion).

After forming in 1986 under the name Mighty Joe Young, the band found immediate success in 1993 after signing with Atlantic Records and releasing their debut album Core (1992) under the STP moniker. The band went on to become one of the most commercially successful bands of the 1990s, releasing four more studio albums: Purple (1994), Tiny Music... Songs from the Vatican Gift Shop (1996), No. 4 (1999) and Shangri-La Dee Da (2001) before separating in 2003, after which the band members partook in various projects, most notably Velvet Revolver and Army of Anyone. STP eventually reconvened in 2008 for a reunion tour, released a new self-titled album in 2010, and have been actively touring since.

While initially displaying a sound typically identified as grunge early on in its career, further releases from the band have shown a variety of influences, including psychedelic rock, bossa nova and classic rock. The band's evolution throughout the 1990s and early 2000s involved several tumultuous periods of commercial highs and lows, brought about in part by Weiland's well-publicized struggles with drug addiction.

wiki.content: Thank You is a greatest hits collection released by the American rock band Stone Temple Pilots on November 11, 2003, by Atlantic Records. There are two versions of the compilation, one that only contains a music CD and another that also features a DVD with live performances, bootlegs, and music videos spanning the band's career. perplexity.description:
Thank You is a greatest hits compilation by Stone Temple Pilots, released on November 11, 2003, by Atlantic Records, encapsulating the band's dominant run in the 1990s alternative rock and hard rock scenes. Spanning 15 tracks drawn primarily from their multi-platinum albums Core (1992), Purple (1994), and Tiny Music... Songs from the Vatican Gift Shop (1996), with selections from No. 4 (1999), it showcases the group's evolution from grunge-infused heaviness to glam-tinged experimentation. Standouts like the riff-driven "Sex Type Thing" and "Wicked Garden" from Core deliver raw hard rock power, while "Plush," "Interstate Love Song," and "Big Empty" from Purple highlight melodic hooks and Scott Weiland's charismatic, versatile vocals that propelled STP to arena status.

The collection's significance lies in its commercial endurance, selling over a million copies and affirming the band's status as 1990s rock titans despite lineup shifts and Weiland's personal struggles. Tracks such as the downtrodden "Creep" and the cruising "Interstate Love Song" exemplify STP's knack for blending brooding introspection with radio-ready anthems, influencing countless guitarists with monster riffs and dynamic shifts. Critically, it retroactively solidified their legacy amid initial grunge comparisons to Pearl Jam and Alice in Chains, with the glam frenzy of "Big Bang Baby" revealing broader stylistic range. Thank You remains a definitive entry point for fans, distilling the essence of STP's hard rock prowess and cultural impact.
